logline: A heavy metal word, READY, travels from a humming office machine to a professional's desk, where two different prepared outputs reveal which work is still unfinished.
committed_angle_executed: In the KGS workflows described by AWS, the machine's finished output is still unfinished professional work.
cold_open_first_three_seconds: Extreme macro: a small office output slot ejects a finished report, then a ludicrously heavy metal READY label descends toward it. The label almost fills the frame. Before it lands, the camera slides sideways to show its empty trailing recess: READY... for what? The machine is faceless and schematic. No seal, approval mark or final-contract text appears.
explainer_spectacle: Make the distinction a comparison of visible operations rather than a statistical claim. DORA gathers and arranges existing record tabs; the separate Jumpstarter apparatus assembles draft prose sections from inputs. In Act 3 the professional performs different actions on those two kinds of material. The big reveal changes the destination of READY, not the reported duration of a task.

hero.use: One persistent bevelled READY type slug, clearly an editorial word-object. It is never a real software control or an approval stamp.

supporting.use: Neutral schematic DORA machine, restaged to show retrieval and prebuilt logic with labels. Do not reuse its previous missing-pipe claim or pressure/strain story.
Workshop rail/port environment for the two clearly independent workflow demonstrations.
Distinct records-intake and professional-review interiors, staged with different camera orientation, depth and work surfaces.
Supporting review prop. Its pen never signs; a parameterized edit gesture may underline or move schematic text, with draft status retained.
Generic faceless professional hand checks source tabs and refines a draft. No cultural or corporate identity is assigned to the hand.
Physical identity and source plates; company names arrive before abbreviations.
Kodiak-region corporate connection on a wall map. No cash arrows or cultural imagery.
Persistent KGS ANNOUNCEMENT or AWS CASE STUDY attribution, with earlier Army scope on mechanism scenes.
Supporting document material only, never the hero or notebook. Clearly distinct report and FIRST DRAFT outputs.
Source-tab and draft-section reveals, avoiding a whole-film notebook format.
Final source and music credits after the button.

shelf_first_cast.small_reusable_extensions_if_needed: Expose a generic labeled document-section arrangement and a pen edit gesture while preserving PenAndDocument's no-signature behavior. Grow existing props, don't add a humanoid AI or a generic server mascot.
shelf_first_cast.freshness: Last heroes were FlightCrate and Sheet. This hero is machined typography. Copper, petrol green, warm stone and ink replace both the clinic cream/spruce/berry palette and the lilac/citron notebook world.

sets.description: Low-angle office output bay with deep receding cabinets and a warm illuminated desktop; generic office, not a claimed federal room.
A cutaway workshop with independent retrieval and drafting stations, clear space between them and source plates. Uses MeasurementField ports and rails as schematic staging.
Wide oblique professional desk with source tabs to one side and draft sections to the other; physically separate from the mechanism workshop.
A wall-mounted Alaska map and two corporate nameplates establish Koniag ownership of KGS and the Kodiak-region connection.

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: The READY slug descends toward a newly produced report. Its too-heavy landing is anticipated and withheld. Plant what READY actually completes.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY suspended over the machine's output

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: A camera pullback ties the READY slug to the story's fresh source: Koniag Government Services' September 11th Wingman announcement, then the Koniag parent nameplate and Kodiak map pin. The slug becomes a leaning question marker beside the announcement.

Three labeled office drawers fan open for contracting, logistics and financial management. Match-cut the contracting drawer into the explicitly earlier AWS Army example. Current Wingman and earlier DORA don't share a false deployment timeline.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY rides the camera-facing drawer lip

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: A generic UEI token enters an email subject. DORA's visible API paths retrieve labeled SAM.gov record tabs. A deliberately small input makes several organized record tabs arrive, with no implied database count or invented private records.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY seated beside DORA's output bay

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: Prebuilt-logic guides line up the tabs into a report. The camera reveals a separate station beside it: Jumpstarter's inputs produce FIRST DRAFT sections through a clearly labeled LLM/Bedrock drafting mechanism. Plant the second question: why will these two finished-looking outputs need different attention?
scene_treatment.object_state: READY bridging the space between two separate outputs

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: Give the useful accomplishment full weight: an assembled report and an editable draft both exist. Faceless guides straighten the materials without strain or error. The two outputs move independently toward the same generic professional desk; there is no DORA-to-Jumpstarter pipeline.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY carried with the two-output comparison into the desk set

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: A professional hand fans the DORA report's attached source tabs, then visually traces a cited tab back to the assembled report. The report is already useful material, yet a review operation remains visible. Show no verdict, error, timer or fatigue.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY rests sideways at the professional's work edge

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: The same generic professional brings the pen to Jumpstarter's persistent FIRST DRAFT page. A schematic paragraph block moves or is refined, not corrected for an invented factual defect. Pay the secondary loop at 78 seconds: one output has source records to check; the other has generated language to refine.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY rotates so its empty trailing recess faces the viewer

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: At 94 seconds the word-object finally seats in a larger desk legend: READY FOR REVIEW. This pays the primary loop. Both source-backed report and editable draft retain their visible material states; the professional is still engaged. The reveal identifies a real handoff without depicting a final award.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY seated within READY FOR REVIEW

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: Return to KGS's current Wingman announcement and the Koniag/Kodiak corporate connection. A modest sourced annotation states that this announcement doesn't quantify Alaska returns. Leave the capable office mechanism visible in a neighboring inset; no missing-money gag or accusation.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY FOR REVIEW legend sits beside the corporate source plates

scene_treatment.dramatic_job: Loop back to the output bay composition, now widened enough to include the active professional desk beyond it. The READY slug is correctly seated in its review legend. Button at roughly 113 seconds; final credits occupy the remaining tail.
scene_treatment.object_state: READY remains correctly qualified while the next prepared output arrives

escalation: The first three scenes make READY a concrete question, locate the named Alaska company and move from current announcement to prior evidence. Scenes four to six open the machinery and clearly separate record retrieval from generative drafting. Scenes seven and eight make the professional's different review actions visible. Scene nine resolves what the machine has finished; scenes ten and eleven return that understanding to the current Alaska business story.
earned_turn: The machine successfully produced the material. The professional then works on it in the ways the source describes. READY was an output state all along; the delayed phrase FOR REVIEW names the next job without manufacturing an AI failure.

button.line: When the output's ready, which job is finished?
button.image: The READY slug rests within READY FOR REVIEW as the camera holds both a working output slot and a professional's active desk. No approval stamp lands.

timed_sight_gags.gag: The tiny machine output is followed by a comically overbuilt metal READY label, as though one little report requires industrial lettering. The object is editorial metaphor, not a literal product feature.
Three office drawers open in a stately fan, then the last one gives a tiny extra shimmy to line its label up. Generic furniture choreography supplies the joke; no worker or community is mocked.
A source tab arrives slightly overenthusiastically, springs past its guide, then settles into alignment. This is physical cartoon overshoot, not a false retrieval or data error.
The heavy READY slug tries to look complete by sitting squarely on the desk, then a routine page turn leaves it at a harmless comic tilt. The professional's work continues unaffected.

act3_test.name: The desk after the output slot
act3_test.strongest_fair_case_against_angle: These are already concrete, useful preparation outputs; saying they are unfinished could dismiss work that the machines actually completed.
act3_test.drawn_at_full_strength: First show each output successfully assembled and ready to handle. Then draw source-tab checking and draft refinement as affirmative professional actions. The machines haven't failed; they finished a smaller job than the whole professional process.
act3_test.not_a_repeat: Act 2 answers how the material is made. Act 3 answers what kind of work can now be done with it, with two different visible actions.

throughline_object.identity: Single heavy READY word-object with one bevelled nick preserved across views; not a document and not a software button.
five_states: seated within READY FOR REVIEW at payoff and button

loops.promise: What does this machine's READY actually finish?
loops.payoff: The slug seats in READY FOR REVIEW while the professional works, revealing a completed preparation task and an unfinished professional task.

loops.promise: Why can't these two prepared outputs be treated as the same kind of material?
loops.payoff: One invites source-record checking; the other requires refinement of generated language. The distinct tools were already named before the midpoint.

retention_plan.padding_test: A 90-second cut would lose the space needed to credit successful preparation and then show actual source-described review, leaving the film to equate a produced page with completed professional work. Keep only the source tracing, draft refinement and READY FOR REVIEW resolution; none needs an invented error, waiting queue or second explanation of the API machinery.

feasibility: The pitch uses shelf typography, records machinery, a rail environment, paper interiors and hand/pen props. No new hero drawing is needed. Custom copy and compositing are essential; label density must be tested at phone scale. The only potential library extension is an editing gesture that never signs or approves. All mechanism imagery is marked schematic and tied to the correct source state.
